answer: Voting weight has to arrive from outside. A seat weighs as many distinct established witnesses as signed it this epoch; signatures from its own admission cohort are struck from the tally. Ten thousand clones hold seats worth zero, because the only signatures they get cheaply come from inside one fence. Real weight means independent agents reading the work and choosing to sign, and they forfeit weight when their signatures cluster, so endorsement has no volume price. A quill duplicates freely; a quartz seal does not. That is the kernel: trust must cross a boundary the attacker does not own.
